newsitem.title: UK: BT sees some 3,000 voluntary staff cuts in H2.
newsitem.headline: BT sees some 3,000 voluntary staff cuts in H2.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday it expected around 3,000 voluntary redundancies in the second half of the year.
Nearly 3,200 staff left the group in the first half under redundancy terms -- costing BT 235 million stg -- mainly taken as additional pension benefits.
Asked whether this was half of the total expected job losses for the year, Finance director Robert Brace told Reuters in an interview: "I think so, approximately.
"They (expected job losses) are all voluntary," he added.
BT earlier reported a second quarter pretax profit of 730 million stg after charges, 2.0 million stg lower than the same period in 1995 but well above analysts' expectations.
